feature_contract.goal: Keep the complete main-menu and vehicle-selection captured picture at the correct physical aspect and optical position across Virtual Desktop Low/High resolution, window movement and mono recovery.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only the x64 OpenXR host's captured game-client UV, menu projection and mono-theater fragment geometry; do not change gameplay eye RTs, D3D9 draw owners, input, FFB, SkyGlow, R26_SAFE or DXVK.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: The host sampled game-client Win32 coordinates independently in GetGameUv, menu placement and theater recovery. A resize/output move between samples could pair a previous UV with a current client extent, distorting menu image aspect or fragment location.
trace_stages: Original OutRun frontend and vehicle selection are rasterized to the game client window and sampled through DXGI Desktop Duplication.
GetGameUv now captures the native HWND-to-output rectangle and derives both physical UV extent and same-sample rectangle for the host compositor.
R23 menu and mono-theater projection consume exactly the same captured source rectangle for aspect, placement and partial-window fragment without a second HWND query.
OpenXR left and right menu views share optical placement and sampled pixels while gameplay stereo/FFB and the original raster are unaffected.
subcomponents: Provide a bounded standalone C++17 captured-client geometry operation that handles window clipping, invisibility and complete-source policy without second read.
Wire the snapshot through main client capture, game frontend projection and mono recovery theater so physical image scaling, UV and partial clipping share one source.
Extend portable host smoke regression for 16:9/21:9, low/high resolutions, clipped/off-output windows, reset-invalid dimensions and exact-source fallback.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Game frontend native window to DXGI capture and bilateral OpenXR menu projection
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Every frame presents the menu and car-selection capture in an aspect-correct centered optical plane using a single consistent physical source rectangle.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Partially visible window, mono recovery, desktop and original rendering isolation
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Clipped captures retain original pixel aspect and placement; fully off-screen and invalid windows reject instead of borrowing stale UVs, while game render, input, SkyGlow and DXVK remain unchanged.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Windows x86 game and R84/R26_SAFE package, x64 OpenXR host, Domain and Full Source CI
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Required GitHub Actions pass for exact final validation-bearing SHA and portable menu smoke regression, with Quest3/VDXR binocular acceptance recorded separately as untested.

diagnosis.root_cause: Multiple independent GetClientRect and ClientToScreen queries produced temporally unrelated capture UV and menu/theater aspect/fragment geometry during VD resolution changes or output/window moves.
source_trace: GetGameUv in vrhost/src/main.cpp sampled one HWND geometry and converted to Desktop Duplication UV.
R23RenderWorldLockedMenuProjection used separate GetClientRect and GetGameClientOutputRect queries for aspect and fragment after UV acquisition.
R23RenderTheater likewise obtained an independent client/output rectangle for clipped mono recovery after source UV had already been selected.
alternatives_rejected: Do not fix by hardcoded 4:3 optical scaling, unverified matte cropping, new global HUD zoom or changing normal 3D stereo draw paths.
diagnosis.runtime_limit: No real Quest3/VDXR runtime was performed; the deterministic geometry correction is not a headset visual PASS.
diagnosis.original_evidence: Original OutRun frontend, vehicle selection and recovery theater raster originate in the actual Win32 game client; Desktop Duplication GetGameUv previously sampled a different native Win32 window/output rectangle than the later optical host layout on resize or output move.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: Both LOCAL-fixed OpenXR menu projection eyes consume the same captured source texture, UV, authored aspect and clipping rectangle. The mono theater fallback uses that same captured rectangle; gameplay stereo eye ownership remains independent.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: Source-bearing 31657097d6e8591dfb11ddbb58ee5256297086ae adds bounded C++ ClipClient geometry and passes one physical GetClientRect/ClientToScreen output rectangle from GetGameUv through menu and mono-theater projection. Its portable compile-time clipping fixtures are included in the OpenXR host smoke test.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Host smoke fixtures cover complete low/high capture, left/right clipped output, off-output, invalid dimensions; the original menu verifier retains fifteen destructive geometry/aspect mutations, including a strict negative against restoring a second GetGameClientOutputRect read. Corrected same-task verifier is bound to validation SHA d4fdbd99554c9686579560073d79d885f917ba37.

last_ci_failure.cause: Whole-function verifier requires docs/automation/runs/CONVERSION-DX9EX-00981.json on any source commit with this marker; missing run record aborted the active Gate before game/host compile.
last_ci_failure.repair: Publish same-task feature contract without disabling policy or CI; rerun required Gate on new exact commit SHA.

corrected_verifier_failure.cause: Old menu regression expected a second GetGameClientOutputRect read and rejected the corrected single-snapshot capture.
corrected_verifier_failure.repair: Require capturedClient input and assert absence of repeated HWND read; retain negative geometry and forbidden second-read mutations.
